verdict.rationale: Rootly's own docs describe Alert Deduplication, which collapses repeat events from the same monitor onto a single open alert using a stable identifier, so the responder sees a count climb instead of being paged again. The alerts overview also states that Rootly groups related alerts together before routing them, which covers both halves of the story. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of related-alert grouping logic (only a single line mentions it), and independent or hands-on corroboration that grouping and dedup actually reduce pages in practice.

support.subject: As an SRE, duplicate and related alerts are deduplicated and grouped so one incident pages one human, not fifty

citations.quote: Collapse repeat events from the same monitor into a single open Rootly alert using a stable identifier, so responders aren't paged twice.
Alert Deduplication collapses those repeat events onto a single open alert, so the responder sees the count climbing instead of getting paged again.
Rootly deduplicates repeats, groups related alerts together, routes each one to the right team
